question: does supervised direction contrast fix the direction error without paying for it in entities or state

arms.ctl: mixed pools unchanged (aug-r1 experiment block of 12 rows)
arms.dir: the same pools with that 12-row block replaced by six direction pairs

base: mix (f84a7adf) for both arms; the start arm is evaluated alongside

pairDesign.perPair: same two entities and same relation; one row names the place, the other names the actor
pairDesign.distinguishable: the two rows differ in the name field and in the value, so the input alone tells which direction is wanted; nothing maps two different answers to the same input
pairDesign.targets: both keep the two entities, the relation and the state
pairDesign.ids: the six pairs reuse the same pairId slots as the block they replace, so the sampler draws the same id sequence

rolepairLocation.rule: pass at least 5 of 6, direction errors at most 1, entity losses at most 1

rolepairPossessor.rule: pass at least 5 of 6 and no part replaced

namepair.rule: pass at least 10 of 12 and at least 4 of 6 on the without-name side

regression.noNewFactLoss: any new human-confirmed fact loss on cf24/final24/moved24 fails the round; the start arm already carries t21:f0
regression.language: not above the start arm (2 on cf24)

stopRule: if the direction improves while entity or state losses grow, the incremental continuation route stops here and the evidence is summarised for a different technical approach; no further per-case patching
sides: possessor and location results are reported separately
